question.prompt: Design a scalable multi-channel notification system capable of sending billions of push notifications, SMS, and emails daily.
expectedPoints: Channel segregation (APNs/FCM for push, Twilio for SMS, Sendgrid/SES for email)
Asynchronous queueing via message brokers (Kafka or RabbitMQ)
User notification preferences and opt-out rate limits
Idempotency and deduplication to avoid double sends
Priority queues for critical notifications (2FA OTP) vs marketing campaigns
commonMistakes: Synchronous calls to third-party providers causing gateway timeout
No rate limiting on marketing blasts causing third-party throttling

transcript: Candidate: A notification system needs to support multiple channels: mobile push, SMS, and email. The core challenge is decoupling notification requests from actual delivery because third-party providers like APNs or Twilio can have latency or outages. We should put an API service behind a load balancer that validates incoming requests and checks user preferences in a database. Then the API publishes messages to Kafka topics partitioned by channel: push-topic, email-topic, sms-topic. Background worker pools consume from these topics and call the respective vendor APIs. If a vendor call fails, the worker retries with exponential backoff and sends persistent failures to a dead-letter queue. We also need priority queues so that urgent OTP codes aren't stuck behind bulk promotional emails. However, I haven't fully worked out deduplication if Kafka produces duplicate messages.
notes: Good asynchronous queue architecture with dead-letter queue and priority separation. Acknowledged gap in message deduplication / idempotency.
